referenceImages.title: Stone Chariot in the Vittala Temple with Intact Brick Superstructure
referenceImages.creator: Colonel Alexander John Greenlaw (1818–1870), 60th Native Infantry, Madras Army
referenceImages.processMedium: Waxed-paper calotype negative (30 x 40 cm negative; 1910 exhibition print)
referenceImages.repositoryArchive: Alkazi Collection of Photography (ACP 98.48.0001) / Victoria and Albert Museum (1910 Prints)
referenceImages.archivalIdentifier: Alkazi Collection ACP 98.48.0001 / V&A Indian Dept 1910
referenceImages.viewpointAndAngle: Oblique frontal elevation from northwest across the Vittala courtyard
visibleArchitecturalFeatures: Conclusive proof of stepped pyramidal brick-and-mortar Dravidian vimana superstructure resting on the flat stone roof.
Visual profile of tiered tower tapering to a domical sikhara and terminal kalasa finial.
Definitive absence of guardian elephant sculptures in front of the entrance steps in 1856.
Chariot entrance balustrades showing pre-existing damage where draft animals stood.
Four granite wheels and molded plinth in authentic 19th-century courtyard soil level.

evidenceClassification.exactNumericalHeight: UNSUPPORTED (Unmeasured prior to loss; estimated proportionally)

referenceImages.reconstructionUtility: Primary historical baseline for the existence, stepped profile, and height-to-width proportion (~1:1 height relative to granite body) of the lost vimana superstructure.
referenceImages.usageWarning: Calotype paper grain obscures micro-level stucco reliefs. Superstructure massing is verified, but specific figural deity reliefs must not be speculatively invented.

referenceImages.title: Temple of Vithoba with an Idol Car of Stone
referenceImages.creator: Dr. Andrew Charles Brisbane Neill (1814–1891), Surgeon, Madras Medical Service
referenceImages.processMedium: Albumen print from calotype negative (26.2 x 34.9 cm image on 43.0 x 58.0 cm mount)
referenceImages.viewpointAndAngle: Northwest oblique three-quarter perspective showing front steps and northern chariot flank
visibleArchitecturalFeatures: Stepped brick-and-mortar vimana superstructure crowning the chariot flat roof.
Independent photographic corroboration of the multi-tiered superstructure silhouette.
Definitive absence of the modern guardian stone elephants in front of the staircase.
Granite wheels, stone axles, and molded adhisthana plinth in authentic 19th-century state.

referenceImages.reconstructionUtility: Vital cross-verification source independently corroborating Greenlaw 1856 regarding the existence and visual massing of the brick superstructure and the absence of elephants.
referenceImages.usageWarning: Like Greenlaw 1856, oblique perspective foreshortens the southern and eastern faces. Rear western elevation is obscured.

referenceImages.title: Stone Chariot, Hampi (Present-Day High-Resolution Ground Truth)
referenceImages.creator: Ankit Darsi
referenceImages.processMedium: High-resolution digital photography (Nikon DSLR, RAW capture)
referenceImages.viewpointAndAngle: Oblique northwest perspective capturing the north flank and entrance steps, aligning with the 1856 archival angle
visibleArchitecturalFeatures: Sub-millimeter granite surface texture of surviving adhisthana plinth, moldings, and relief friezes.
Intact concentric floral carvings on front and rear north wheels.
Modern addition: Two guardian stone elephants flanking entrance steps.
Surviving in-situ relief carvings of draft animal hindquarters on balustrades behind elephants.
Flat top roof slab with bare masonry platform where superstructure once rested.
